==Problem==

Four numbers are written in a row. The average of the first two is <imath>21,</imath> the average of the middle two is <imath>26,</imath> and the average of the last two is <imath>30.</imath> What is the average of the first and last of the numbers?

<imath>\textbf{(A) } 24 \qquad \textbf{(B) } 25 \qquad \textbf{(C) } 26 \qquad \textbf{(D) } 27 \qquad \textbf{(E) } 28</imath>

==Solution 1 (Arithmetic)==

Note that the sum of the first two numbers is <imath>21\cdot2=42,</imath> the sum of the middle two numbers is <imath>26\cdot2=52,</imath> and the sum of the last two numbers is <imath>30\cdot2=60.</imath>

It follows that the sum of the four numbers is <imath>42+60=102,</imath> so the sum of the first and last numbers is <imath>102-52=50.</imath> Therefore, the average of the first and last numbers is <imath>50\div2=\boxed{\textbf{(B) } 25}.</imath>

~MRENTHUSIASM

==Solution 2 (Algebra)==

Let <imath>a,b,c,</imath> and <imath>d</imath> be the four numbers in that order. We are given that
<cmath>\begin{align*}
\frac{a+b}{2} &= 21, &(1) \\
\frac{b+c}{2} &= 26, &(2) \\
\frac{c+d}{2} &= 30, &(3)
\end{align*}</cmath>
and we wish to find <imath>\frac{a+d}{2}.</imath>

We add <imath>(1)</imath> and <imath>(3),</imath> then subtract <imath>(2)</imath> from the result: <cmath>\frac{a+d}{2}=21+30-26=\boxed{\textbf{(B) } 25}.</cmath>
~MRENTHUSIASM

==Solution 3==

Let <imath>a,b,c,</imath> and <imath>d</imath> be the four numbers in that order. We are given that
<cmath>\begin{align*}
\frac{a+b}{2} &= 21, &(1) \\
\frac{b+c}{2} &= 26, &(2) \\
\frac{c+d}{2} &= 30, &(3)
\end{align*}</cmath>
and we wish to find <imath>\frac{a+d}{2}.</imath>

If we subtract <imath>(2)</imath> from <imath>(3)</imath>, we get <cmath>\frac{c+d}{2}-\frac{b+c}{2}=\frac{d-b}{2}=4.</cmath>
So if we multiply by <imath>2</imath> then we get <imath>d=b+8.</imath> Looking at our question: <cmath>\frac{a+d}{2}=\frac{a+b+8}{2}=\frac{a+b}{2}+\frac{8}{2}=21+4=\boxed{\textbf{(B) } 25}.</cmath>

~funnyarmadillo58_aops

==Solution 4==
Let’s label these <imath>4</imath> numbers <imath>A</imath>,<imath>B</imath>,<imath>C</imath>, and <imath>D</imath>. 


<imath>A</imath> + <imath>B</imath> = <imath>42</imath>

<imath>B</imath> + <imath>C</imath> = <imath>52</imath>

<imath>C</imath> + <imath>D</imath> = <imath>60</imath>


We can use elimination to solve this: 
<imath>A</imath> - <imath>C</imath> = <imath>-10</imath>

and since 

<imath>D</imath> + <imath>C</imath> = <imath>60</imath>

then

<imath>A</imath> + <imath>D</imath> = <imath>50</imath>


Finally, to find the average, divide by <imath>2</imath>. The answer is <imath>25</imath>, or <imath>B</imath>

-OddPeppyBoots
